name: Synaptrel
description: Synaptrel is a synthetic neural velocity compound that temporarily accelerates synaptic transmission in the motor and sensory cortex by saturating sodium-potassium channel regulators, effectively overclocking the nervous system's signal propagation speed. Developed by Helix Biosystems as a bridge product for unaugmented individuals competing in augmented environments, it delivers measurable reflex improvements of 18-30 milliseconds — enough to matter in close-quarters combat against chrome-heavy opponents. It is the pharmaceutical answer to the augmentation gap.
effects: Perception of opponents moving slightly slower
Enhanced fine motor precision under stress
side_effects: Risk of neural overstimulation causing seizure at high doses
Hypersensitivity to sensory input — bright light and loud sound become painful
Chronic use causes permanent low-grade tremor
cultural_context: Synaptrel is the great equalizer of the GLMZ underworld — the chemical that lets an unaugmented Shelf runner stand a chance against a corporate enforcer with military chrome reflexes. It is also a quiet political statement. The augmentation gap between tiers is one of the most visible and resented inequalities in GLMZ; Synaptrel is how the unaugmented refuse to simply accept being slower. Helix markets it carefully, aware that its existence makes augmentation manufacturers uncomfortable.
story_hooks: A tournament circuit for unaugmented fighters has banned Synaptrel, but the testing methods are easily defeated — a runner is hired to investigate whether the champion is clean or bought.
Helix Biosystems is sitting on a next-generation formulation that would close the gap almost entirely; Lazarus has been quietly acquiring their research staff.
A Shelf kid running Synaptrel for the first time reacts fast enough to survive an ambush that should have killed her — and the people who sent the ambush want to know what she's on.
